scenes.headline: How Baphomet 1.1 was searched, not trained
scenes.sub: Eight fine-tunes of one Qwen, eight weights to tune
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Ozias! Baphomet one point one was made without training. Here is the search, and the held-out test.

steps.term: Task vector: a fine-tune's change from the base
steps.say: Every parent is the same Qwen base plus a change. Draw each change as an arrow, and the arrow's tip is the parent.
The search starts from each parent alone, from their plain average, and from random mixes.
Then it settles on one weight per parent. The Qwen three point eight distill gets the most.
Add the scaled arrows head to tail and you land on the merge. Eight numbers, the same for every layer.
The search is EvoGM. Seed a population: the parents, their average, random mixes.

steps.term: Fitness: the score the search maximises
steps.say: Score each candidate on a hundred and ten questions. An answer cut off at the token cap counts as wrong.
Split them. The top thirty percent are winners.
A small network learns to move losers toward winners, and proposes the next candidates.
Then the best mixes become the new parents.
That loop, in the paper's own drawing.

scenes.title: Fitness on the 110 items
scenes.say: On those questions the merge scores seventy-six point four. Its best parent, sixty-eight point six.

steps.say: The weights it found: point five nine on the Qwen three point eight distill.

steps.caption: 0.59, 0.30 and 0.20; five agent parents near zero
steps.say: The five agent fine-tunes get almost nothing.

states.say: Now the held-out test. One point one gets a hundred and forty-three of a hundred and eighty.

states.term: McNemar test: only the items two models disagree on
states.say: Against one point oh, they disagree on seventeen. Ten go one way, seven the other. A coin does that often.

left.title: Baphomet 1.0
items: 28 answers cut off at the cap
left.say: One point oh runs out of room on twenty-eight answers.

right.title: Baphomet 1.1
right.say: One point one is cut off on eighteen and writes about half as much. Of the ten extra answers it finishes, seven are wrong.
